overall: The AG found the Great Barrington Board of Assessors violated the Open Meeting Law by posting insufficiently specific executive session notices (wrong purpose cited), failing to keep accurate minutes, and responding late to the complaint; it ordered compliance and corrected minutes.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the notices for the July 20 and September 13 executive sessions lacked sufficient specificity, including a wrong purpose cited and unexplained shorthand.
allegations.key_passage: Therefore, the notices for the July 20 and September 13 meetings did not satisfy the requirements of the Open Meeting Law.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the minutes of the July 20 and September 13 meetings, including executive session discussion of abatement applications, were not sufficiently detailed.
allegations.key_passage: The Board violated the Open Meeting Law in failing to prepare accurate minutes of both the open and executive session portions of the meetings of July 20 and September 13.

allegations.summary: The Board responded to the complaint more than two weeks after the 14-business-day deadline; the letter addresses this in a footnote.
allegations.key_passage: the failure to timely respond to a complaint is itself a violation of the Open Meeting Law.

remedy: Immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law.
Amend and approve minutes for the July 20 and September 13 meetings, consistent with the guidance in the letter, and certify to the AG that it has done so within 40 days of the letter.
remedy_passage: We order the Board's immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law and caution the Board that a determination by our office of a similar violation in the future may be considered evidence of intent to violate the Open Meeting Law. In addition, we order the Board to amend and approve minutes for the July 20 and September 13 meetings, consistent with the guidance provided above, and to certify to this office that it has done so within 40 days from the date of this letter.
